newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom analyst forecasts too low - report.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom analyst forecasts too low - report.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG is budgeting for current year earnings per share nearly 20 percent ahead of the existing consensus of analyst expectations, a German business magazine said on Friday.

The magazine Capital, which said it had gained access to internal financial planning documents prepared by Telekom financial chief Joachim Kroeske, said the group was forecasting earnings per share 18 percent above those forecast by the major banks for this year.

It added that the internal study, which covers the years 1997 to 2001, shows Kroeske's current year cash flow per share forecast is five percent higher than that expected by analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which target 8.32 marks per share for 1997, the magazine said.
Internally, sales were seen increasing at an average five percent a year to 2001, with pre-tax profit quadrupling over the period to reach 20.5 billion marks in 2001, Capital said.
It said that as a result the Deutsche Telekom board, including chairman Ron Sommer, considered the group to be "extremely undervalued" at current share prices.
Deutsche Telekom shares currently trade around 37.70 marks after having risen strongly over the last two weeks as investors, particularly in the U.S., become increasingly interested in the stock.
The group was not immediately available for comment.
